2w Your migration can turn a paying subscriber into a decline. For a recurring payment to work, the network needs to recognize its link to the customer’s original consent. Those identifiers often live inside the current payment setup. Move processors without preserving that chain and an established subscriber can look like a first-time payer. The card has not necessarily changed. The proof that it belongs to a valid recurring agreement may be missing. Network tokens have their own relationship and onboarding dependencies. This is why a processor migration can be more than a routing update, and why active subscriptions become the risk. The migration question is not only: Can we move the cards

Dear Store Owners, all your eggs probably sit in one basket….\
\
Starting your store on Shopify is a good move. But once you scale your subscriptions, all your eggs do sit in one basket. Your customers’ saved cards live inside one company’s account. If that account gets blocked, you can’t get to them.\
\
On Tagada, the saved cards stay yours. If one processor blocks you, you switch to another and keep billing.\
